memory_update.text: AMKR should remain in the node universe as the most direct US-listed OSAT/advanced-packaging overflow candidate, but its thesis must be separated from generic OSAT cyclicality.
FORM should remain in the node universe as an HBM testing-gate candidate because company materials explicitly connect its probe cards to HBM testing and SK hynix.
COHU should remain in the node universe as a low-attention HBM backend test-handler candidate, with direct but currently modest disclosed HBM revenue.

KLIC is a relevant follow-up candidate for a later Layer 1B or Layer 2 pass because thermocompression bonding and advanced packaging tools have explicit HBM/AI packaging links, but the current four-candidate cap prioritized TSM reference plus AMKR/FORM/COHU.

The key falsification test for this node is whether candidate revenue is driven by AI/HBM/advanced packaging intensity rather than only broad memory-cycle beta or semiconductor capital-equipment recovery.

node: HBM, advanced packaging, OSAT, and backend memory-test overflow
summary: Expanded the node from obvious AI accelerator and foundry leaders into US-listed second-order beneficiaries around outsourced advanced packaging, HBM-adjacent wafer/probe testing, backend test handlers, and bonding/advanced-packaging tools. The reference lane is limited to TSM as the capacity anchor. The underfollowed lane prioritizes AMKR, FORM, COHU, and KLIC-like exposures, but candidate count is capped at four, so KLIC is included and AMKR/FORM/COHU are the core discovery assets. Claims are deliberately labeled: direct company product statements are facts; overflow/crowding-out benefits are hypotheses until confirmed by segment revenue, customer concentration, utilization, and backlog disclosures.
